sections.purpose: To non-invasively measure arterial oxygen saturation (SpO₂) and pulse rate using a pulse oximeter as part of clinical pharmacology and pharmacy practice training.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmacology laboratory for clinical monitoring practicals and patient assessment skills training.
procedure: Ensure the pulse oximeter battery is fully charged or insert fresh batteries if applicable.
Turn on the device and verify it passes self-test (screen should show '---' or start-up animation).
Ask the subject to remove nail polish or artificial nails from the finger to be tested.
Ensure the subject's hand is warm — cold fingers reduce perfusion and give inaccurate readings.
Insert the subject's index or middle finger fully into the probe/clip, ensuring the LED emitter faces the fingernail side.
Instruct the subject to hold still and breathe normally.
Allow 10–15 seconds for the reading to stabilize.
Read the SpO₂ percentage and pulse rate from the display.
Normal SpO₂ range: 95–100%; Normal pulse rate: 60–100 bpm at rest.
Note the plethysmography waveform quality if displayed — a poor waveform indicates unreliable readings.
Record values along with subject details, time, and clinical context.
Remove the finger from the probe gently.
Clean the probe with a 70% alcohol swab and allow to dry before storing.
Turn off the device and store in its protective case.
precautions: Ensure the finger is inserted properly — partial insertion leads to inaccurate readings.
Bright ambient light (especially fluorescent or direct sunlight) can interfere with readings — shade the probe if necessary.
Motion artifacts can produce spurious readings — ensure the subject remains still.
Poorly perfused fingers (cold hands, peripheral vascular disease) may give falsely low SpO₂ readings.
Carbon monoxide poisoning can cause falsely normal SpO₂ despite actual hypoxia.
Dark nail polish (especially blue, black, green) can interfere with readings.
Do not use the device on subjects with severe peripheral oedema or Raynaud's disease without clinical supervision.
Service the device and replace probes as per manufacturer's maintenance schedule.
Values below 90% SpO₂ indicate hypoxia — refer immediately for clinical evaluation.
